interest: Documents 1930s US tracking of Japan's covert naval buildup, including the Hiei's rearming, the secret Yamato-class, and overseas fuel/sub procurement.
overview: This file comprises the Department of State's cumulative 'List of Papers' (docket sheets and purport register) for decimal file 894.34 (Japan: Equipment and Supplies, including naval construction, purchase and sale of vessels) covering the years 1930 through 1940. It systematically indexes diplomatic exchanges, naval attaché despatches, and inter-departmental communications regarding Japan's naval expansion under and following the expiration of the Washington and London Naval Treaties. The sheets record formal notifications transmitted by the Japanese Embassy in Washington detailing keel-layings and completions of battleships, aircraft carriers, cruisers, destroyers, and submarines, alongside U.S. Navy Department and consular reports tracking clandestine Japanese capital ship construction (notably rumors of 40,000-to-55,000-ton super-battleships), the controversial remilitarization of the training battleship Hiei, espionage allegations involving battleship plans in Seoul, and worldwide Japanese efforts to acquire naval petroleum, machinery, and raw materials from the United States, Mexico, Argentina, and Europe.

subfiles.about: A cumulative docket and purport register indexing State Department correspondence, diplomatic notifications, intelligence reports, and inter-departmental communications regarding Japanese naval equipment, construction, and supplies between 1930 and 1940.
subfiles.summary: This cumulative 26-page docket sheet records incoming and outgoing communications concerning Japanese naval equipment, warship construction, and strategic supplies from May 1930 through January 1940. It indexes formal diplomatic notes from the Japanese Embassy in Washington announcing keel-layings and completions of capital ships, aircraft carriers, cruisers, destroyers, and submarines under the London Naval Treaty of 1930, alongside U.S. Navy Department and consular reports. Notable subjects tracked in the register include espionage inquiries in Seoul, proposed foreign purchases of Argentine submarines and European armaments, Anglo-American intelligence and diplomatic protests regarding the remilitarization of the battleship Hiei, rumors of post-treaty super-battleships exceeding 35,000 tons, and Japanese government efforts to secure crude oil and industrial machinery in Mexico and the United States.
